target_customer: Developers and small teams who use several AI coding agents
problem: Coding agents forget earlier sessions, so developers re-solve problems and cannot move a session between Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other agents.
business_model: Freemium local-first desktop app and CLI with paid team workspaces (pricing page not read)
product_category: Developer tools, AI agent session search and portability

founders.name: Narayana Aaditya Ganeshkumar
founders.background_notes: YC page says he helped take an open-source Rust project to 30k+ GitHub stars and has engineering, product and organizational psychology background. Employers and education not stated.

founders.name: Nishant Joshi
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as a Rust developer who moved from type-safe payment infrastructure to people search. Employers and education not stated.

technical_complexity.rationale: Translating session transcripts between several agent formats and searching them locally before each prompt is standard engineering with a format-chasing burden; the open source txcript engine is written in Rust.

defensibility.rationale: Format converters and local search are copyable by agent vendors or open-source projects; the open-source txcript engine lowers the barrier further.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Not yet known. Agent vendors own their own session stores and could add history search or import; no acquisition or copy was found as of 2026-11.

market_need_then: Developers were running several coding agents at once in 2025 and 2026 and complaining that context did not carry over; the founders' own launch post frames this as the problem. No spend data found.

identity.visual_style: Minimal, terminal-style mockups, memes on homepage
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual, lowercase headlines such as never solve it twice

branding.community_and_virality: Homepage includes a playful midwit meme; no third-party brand coverage found

brand_strength.rationale: Name is a compound that is easy to say but generic and shared with other products named SkillSync; no independent brand press found.

pivots.from: Engineer discovery tool for finding overlooked engineers on GitHub
pivots.to: Search and portability for agent session history
pivots.why: Not stated; reported by an aggregator summary and a YC launch title that I did not open

outcome_analysis: Skillsync is a two-person Winter 2026 company, active as of 2026-11, with no reported exit or shutdown. It rides the timing tailwind of multi-agent coding, but agent vendors hold the underlying session data and can copy the wedge, so the outcome is too early to read.
notes: A $500K pre-seed from Y Combinator and Character Capital appears only on aggregators (vcbacked, yespress) so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. No dated competitor source near the batch was found, so the list is empty; claude-mem style tools exist but search results were undated. Possible earlier product on engineer discovery per aggregators is unverified. Completeness pass: the 500K March 2026 pre-seed rests on VCBacked and YesPress; VCBacked names only YC, and Character Capital is named by YesPress. No primary confirmation.
